exposure: fetal urinary production rate (FUPR) measured by ultrasound
outcome: length of neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) stay
reduced neonatal urine production rate (<4 mL/kg/h)
cohort: The study included 38 women with singleton pregnancies complicated by preterm premature rupture of membranes (PPROM) occurring at gestational week 24 or later.
finding: Low fetal urinary production rate (FUPR) was associated with clinical chorioamnionitis, longer NICU hospitalization, higher rates of necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC) or intraventricular hemorrhage (IVH), and blood transfusions.
followup_time: The last observation was taken at the end of the neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) stay, which had a variable length.
gest_age: Gestational week 24 or later at the time of PPROM.
